summary.intent: Execute all 9 plans of phase 71 (Share-Invite Security & IPNS Data-Integrity API) in cipher-box using the GSD wave-based parallel execution workflow, orchestrating subagents across 4 dependency-ordered waves with worktree isolation.
summary.outcome: All 9 plans across 4 waves executed, merged, and gated successfully (final: pnpm typecheck green, 894/894 api tests passing); the blocking human-verify checkpoint in plan 71-05 was resolved by driving a live-stack run that confirmed the D-06 concurrent first-publish race yields exactly one 200 and one 409, never a 500; phase verification was starting as the transcript ends.

repo: cipher-box's root `pnpm typecheck` excludes `apps/api tsc --noEmit`, so errors surfaced only by a raw `apps/api tsc --noEmit` run are non-CI-gating and can be legitimately deferred.
Wave 1 of a rename-style phase can intentionally leave TS consumers (sdk/web) broken until Wave 2 fixes them — a full `pnpm typecheck` should not be used as the Wave 1 post-merge gate in that case.
gsd worktree `base-check` reporting reason `baseref-head` means worktrees fork from live HEAD, which lets every wave keep parallel worktree isolation without degrading to sequential across waves.
The gsd tracking-commit helper can report `commit_failed` as a false negative even though the commit actually landed — always verify via `git log`, not the helper's own status.

`codebase-drift` gate flags large advisory 'drift' as baseline noise when `last_mapped_commit: null` (repo never ran `/gsd-map-codebase`) — safe to treat as non-blocking if no phase-modified files are among the flagged items.

sdk-e2e (vitest) does not auto-load `.env`; if `SDK_E2E_SECRET` isn't explicitly exported it falls back to a hardcoded default that can mismatch the API's `TEST_LOGIN_SECRET`, causing an early-suite 401 that cascade-skips all later suites including the target test.
Worktrees don't inherit gitignored `.env` files — must be manually copied in before running e2e suites from a worktree.
`pnpm --filter X test --` wrapping silently drops a `--testPathPattern`-style argument due to double `--`; use `npx jest`/direct test runner invocation instead.
Fresh worktrees lack `node_modules` and built `dist/` for internal packages like `@cipherbox/crypto`; executors must run `pnpm i` plus targeted package builds before tests/typecheck are meaningful.

`requirements.mark-complete` uses the global REQUIREMENTS.md REQ-ID scheme; phase 71 requirements use CONTEXT.md decision-ID naming (D-xx/SC#x), so mark-complete calls against those IDs are silent no-ops (`not_found`), not failures.

A stale compiled API process (`node dist/main.js`, not watch mode) can linger on :3000 from a prior session; using it for live verification would give false results since it lacks the current branch's fixes — must kill and restart from source before trusting a live-stack test.

code.finding: D-05 same-seq CID equivocation guard and D-06 first-publish 23505→409 (ConflictException) translation were added here by plan 71-04.
claimInvite's existing-share branch replaced with a widen-only merge (isWriteUpgrade/isGenerationBump gates) so grants never downgrade write→read (plan 71-07, SC#2).
revokeForItems rewritten from find()+remove() to a single createQueryBuilder().delete() scoped to sharer_id+share_root_ipns_name, mirroring the sibling invite-revoke update block (plan 71-08, SC#5).

E0560 diagnostics referencing old field names after 71-03's rename were stale LSP noise from an intermediate worktree state, not real errors — confirmed clean via `cargo check --all-targets` on the merged tree.
Pre-existing TS2352 error, unchanged vs origin/main and untouched by phase 71 — confirmed non-gating since CI's typecheck script excludes apps/api tsc.

workflow: For multi-wave orchestration, verify a spawned agent's worktree exists (and its config.lock released) before dispatching the next parallel agent in the same wave, to avoid a git config race.

Don't blindly trust a subagent's self-reported test/check results when they conflict with raw diagnostics (e.g. cargo E0560) — settle discrepancies by re-running the check against the merged tree at the post-merge gate.

When a plan includes a blocking human-verify checkpoint requiring a live environment, have the executor author/commit the autonomous portion, pause and return exact reproduction commands, then let the orchestrator (with user approval) drive the live run rather than the subagent.

For trivial checkpoint-continuation work (writing a SUMMARY + one commit), it can be more efficient for the orchestrator to do it directly via `git -C` on the existing worktree rather than spawning another full agent.

friction: Stale/misleading cargo E0560 diagnostics from plan 71-03's subagent required an extra verification pass at Wave 2 post-merge before being ruled out as noise.
gsd tracking-commit helper falsely reported `commit_failed` twice (Wave 1 and Wave 3a) even though the commits had landed, requiring manual git-log verification each time.
A stale compiled API process was already occupying :3000 from a prior session and had to be identified and killed before a trustworthy live-stack test run.

sdk-e2e/API login-secret mismatch (SDK_E2E_SECRET default vs TEST_LOGIN_SECRET) caused a 401 that cascade-skipped the target test on the first live-stack attempt, requiring root-cause investigation before a second, correctly-scoped run.
Worktrees lacked gitignored `.env` files, blocking the live e2e run until manually copied in.
71-08's executor hit a `pnpm --filter test --` wrapper bug that silently drops the test-pattern argument, requiring a workaround (direct npx jest invocation).
